generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The test method `testDuplicateSliceRelease` contains a copy-paste error. The body calls `buf.duplicate().duplicate()` (identical to `testDuplicateDuplicateRelease` in #7P03B) instead of the intended `buf.duplicate().slice()`. As written, this test does not actually exercise the `duplicate().slice()` path at all.

Both new inner classes carry `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation")`, indicating that `SlicedByteBuf` and `DuplicatedByteBuf` are deprecated. Building new public-facing read-only wrappers on top of deprecated base classes will propagate the deprecation concern into the new types and will require another migration when those base classes are eventually removed. Consider whether a shared abstract base or a composition-based approach would be more future-proof, or at minimum add a brief note (e.g., a `// TODO` or a class-level Javadoc remark) explaining why the deprecated parents are still the right choice here.

review_comment: The reason why read-only ByteBuffers are needed in the SslHandler use case is to avoid mutating the buffer. JDK's SSLEngine will mutate the input buffer with an in-place encryption reusing the input buffer unless the buffer is read-only. The support for read-only ByteBuffers in JDK's SSLEngine was added as a result of a bug reported by @chrisvest, more details in comment https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14069#issuecomment-2129279047 .
